title: Groundwater availability, geochemistry, and flow pathways to public-supply wells in the Atlantic Coastal Plain and bedrock aquifers, Aiken County and part of Lexington County, South Carolina, 2015–2019
citation: Campbell, B.G., and Landmeyer, J.E., 2023, Groundwater availability, geochemistry, and flow pathways to public-supply wells in the Atlantic Coastal Plain and bedrock aquifers, Aiken County and part of Lexington County, South Carolina, 2015–2019: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report SIR-2022-5036, map scale 1:800,000.
notes:
Simulated and calibrated model values (MODFLOW hydraulic conductivities, storage, water budgets, flow pathways, future scenarios) are model output and were not recorded. Abstract and overview ranges of field measurements, radium, VOCs and ages (pages 17-20) summarize per-well tables in later packets and were not recorded here. Population, climate, land use and precipitation not recorded. Figure 8 (page 30) is a schematic section, not drawn to scale, of the Aiken-Barnwell area with hydrostratigraphic names (Steed Pond, Floridan-Midville, Dublin-Midville, Meyers Branch, Allendale, Gramling, Appleton); only well labels were recorded. SUBSURFACE: base of ACP sediments about 700 ft NAVD 88 at the Fall Line to about -700 ft NAVD 88 southeastward (page 26); the bedrock modeling limit is the approximate 1,000-ft thickness of crystalline bedrock (page 22).
Table 2 (page 39): 16 public-supply wells and 4 monitoring wells (C3 Cluster site, Aiken State Park) with year installed, land-surface altitude (NGVD 29), total depth and aquifer screened; well names, USGS site ID numbers and pump types are in each label note. USGS site ID numbers encode latitude and longitude but no location is printed, so none was recorded. Table 1 (page 38, streamflow measurement sites) was not recorded (not geologic). Pages 44-63 describe the MODFLOW model, calibration and simulated results (tables 3-6, figures 19-41); these are model values and were not recorded. Page 32 water-level range 91 to 581 ft (NAVD 88) is a summary of model calibration data. SUBSURFACE: only land-surface altitudes and total depths of wells (table 2); no unit tops or bases.
